LTPAC Health IT Collaborative Comment Letter: Proposed rule on Prior Authorization for Drugs
Page 1
Date: June 12, 2026
Submitted via: www.regulations.gov
Administrator Mehmet Oz, M.D.
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
Department of Health and Human Services
P.O. Box 8013
Baltimore, MD 21244-8013
Re: CMS Proposed Rule: Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act; Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs for Medicare Advantage Organizations, Medicaid Managed Care Plans, State Medicaid Agencies, Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) Agencies and CHIP Managed Care Entities, and Issuers of Qualified Health Plans on the Federally-Facilitated Exchanges
Dear Administrator,
The Long-Term Post-Acute Care (LTPAC) Health IT Collaborative ("the Collaborative") submits these comments on the proposed rule on Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs (CMS-0062-P), published in the Federal Register on April 14, 2026 (Vol. 91, No. 71). The Collaborative's members include provider and professional associations and national experts representing nursing facilities, skilled nursing facilities, assisted living, home health, hospice, continuing care retirement communities, rehabilitation services, pharmacy, nursing, and healthcare information systems.
analysis:
## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** LTPAC Health IT Collaborative, contact Michelle Dougherty (Convener), leaders@ltpachit.org
- **Stakeholder type:** Professional Association (multi-sector collaborative representing LTPAC provider associations, vendors, payers, and national experts; members include nursing facilities, SNFs, assisted living, home health, hospice, CCRCs, rehabilitation, pharmacy, nursing, and health IT)
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** Established in 2005; engaged in every major federal health IT and interoperability rulemaking; participated in HITAC May 7, 2026 Affordability Hearing; commented on HTI-2, CMS-0057, CRUSH RFI, NIH AI Strategy RFI; Shelly Spiro cited as emeritus member and HITAC panelist

---

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The LTPAC Health IT Collaborative strongly supports the proposed rule's goals of standardizing electronic PA, reducing administrative burden, and increasing transparency, but argues the rule fails to address the unique clinical, regulatory, and technological context of long-term and post-acute care settings. The Collaborative identifies five imperatives: recognizing LTPAC mandatory care obligations and prohibiting retroactive PA denials; enforcing standards on payers first; developing LTPAC-specific implementation guidance; closing the LTPAC interoperability gap (rooted in 15-year HITECH exclusion); and stratifying public PA metrics by care setting and drug category.

---

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** PA-DRUG-PHARMACY, PA-DRUG-MEDICAL, FHIR-IG-REQUIRED, PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS, API-USAGE-METRICS, HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS, ONC-STANDARDS-UPDATE, GENERAL (RFI responses on lab tests, DMEPOS, AI, workforce)
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** CMS-0062-P; CMS-0057 (2024 Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule); ONC HTI-2 rulemaking; 42 CFR Part A consolidated billing framework; Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 71 (April 14, 2026)
- **Standards referenced:** NCPDP SCRIPT (version 2023011), NCPDP Formulary and Benefit (FB), NCPDP Real-Time Prescription Benefit (RTPB); HL7 FHIR; Da Vinci CRD v2.2.1 STU 2.2; Da Vinci DTR v2.2.0 STU 2.2; Da Vinci PAS v2.2.1 STU 2.2; Da Vinci CDex v2.1.0 STU 2.1; X12N 278; PACIO Project FHIR IGs; TEFCA/QHINs; MDS (Minimum Data Set); OASIS

---

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: LTPAC Mandatory Care Obligations and Retroactive PA Denials**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-PHARMACY, PA-DRUG-MEDICAL, GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify (request new policy)
- **Rationale:** Drug PA in LTPAC is categorically different from community pharmacy PA. LTPAC providers must administer medications before payer authorization is obtained due to federal/state mandatory care obligations. Retroactive denials and retroactive eligibility changes impose direct financial harm on facilities operating on thin margins; PA delays constitute patient safety events.
- **Specific request:** Explicitly recognize LTPAC mandatory care obligations in the final rule preamble; prohibit retroactive PA denials for medications administered under those obligations; establish procedures for prospective PA submission when coverage is uncertain; address retroactive eligibility change interactions in LTPAC-specific guidance.

**Topic 2: NCPDP Standards Support**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-PHARMACY
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** NCPDP SCRIPT, FB, and RTPB are foundational to LTPAC e-prescribing and, once uniformly adopted, have the potential to meaningfully reduce the current fragmented PA landscape (65+ payer web portals, 750+ fax forms, 63+ payers in a single nursing home).
- **Specific request:** Apply requirements to all Medicare and Medicaid subcontractors, not only "impacted payers"; enforce rigorous payer compliance with monitored readiness milestones before provider compliance is required.

**Topic 3: FHIR Da Vinci IG Requirements**
- **Provision ID:** FHIR-IG-REQUIRED, ONC-STANDARDS-UPDATE
- **Position:** Support with modification
- **Rationale:** Da Vinci CRD, DTR, PAS, CDex IGs are integral to the PA ecosystem; HITAC confirmed gaps including lack of LTPAC EHR testing environments, insufficient provider awareness, and incomplete state Medicaid FHIR questionnaire digitization.
- **Specific request:** Include LTPAC EHR and pharmacy system vendors in publicly available ePA testing environments; require LTPAC enrollment sites in ONC innovation programs (EHIgnite, LEAP); support state Medicaid centralized FHIR questionnaire development; require compatibility with PACIO Project FHIR IGs.

**Topic 4: Payer-First Standards Enforcement**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-PHARMACY, FHIR-IG-REQUIRED
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** HITAC confirmed payer compliance with CMS-0057 APIs is not expected to be complete until end of 2026; if standards are applied simultaneously to payers and providers, LTPAC providers must comply with both CMS requirements and each payer's non-standard legacy requirements, compounding burden.
- **Specific request:** Establish monitored payer readiness milestones with publicly available API testing environments before provider compliance requirements take effect; extend requirements to all Medicare/Medicaid subcontractors.

**Topic 5: PA Decision Timeframes**
- **Provision ID:** PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS
- **Position:** Support with additions
- **Rationale:** LTPAC patients experience the most severe consequences of PA delays; standardized, shortened timeframes applied uniformly across all payer types would improve patient safety and care quality.
- **Specific request:** Apply shortest clinically appropriate timeframes consistently across all payer types; require all impacted payers to honor emergency supply provisions (minimum 72-hour supply) when a PA decision is pending, including in-facility medication administration in LTPAC settings.

**Topic 6: Patient/Resident Notification for Cognitively Impaired**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DENIAL-REASONS, GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** A substantial proportion of LTPAC residents have dementia or other cognitive conditions; standard patient notification designed for cognitively intact outpatients is inappropriate.
- **Specific request:** Require PA notices to be directed to legally recognized surrogate decision-makers; require facility-level receipt of PA decisions as primary notification channel in SNF and LTPAC settings; design consumer-facing tools for accessibility, low health literacy, and caregiver use.

**Topic 7: Public Reporting of PA Metrics**
- **Provision ID:** API-USAGE-METRICS
- **Position:** Support with modification
- **Rationale:** Aggregate plan-level metrics will not reveal disparities that LTPAC patients experience; stratified reporting is necessary for accountability and identification of patterned denials.
- **Specific request:** Require PA metrics stratified by care setting (including LTPAC), drug category (specialty, antipsychotics, opioids, anticoagulants, biologics), payer type and plan, and standardized denial reason codes distinguishing procedural from clinical necessity denials; establish a binding automation target (90%+ of PA submissions conformant with Burden Reduction APIs) with financial consequences for non-compliance.

**Topic 8: HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS**
- **Provision ID:** HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS
- **Position:** Support with caveats
- **Rationale:** FHIR as HIPAA transaction standard for PA modernizes long-overdue administrative transactions; however, LTPAC EHR and pharmacy system vendors will need targeted implementation support due to older systems and limited interoperability infrastructure.
- **Specific request:** Develop targeted FHIR/HIPAA transition support resources specifically for LTPAC EHR and pharmacy system vendors; preserve extension and flexibility mechanisms for small plans and state Medicaid agencies during transition.

**Topic 9: LTPAC Interoperability Gap**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL, FHIR-IG-REQUIRED
- **Position:** Modify (request new funding/policy)
- **Rationale:** Only 17% of hospitals routinely send interoperable health information to LTPAC providers; only 8% routinely receive it; the LTPAC sector was excluded from HITECH Act funding, creating a 15-year technology investment gap that rulemaking alone cannot close.
- **Specific request:** Dedicate funding and technical assistance for LTPAC EHR and pharmacy system vendors; integrate LTPAC into TEFCA-based ePA exchange via QHINs; establish payer obligation to maintain demographic records consistent with LTPAC provider EHR data to address the ~30% PA submission failure rate from demographic misalignment.

**Topic 10: RFI — Lab Tests and DMEPOS**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Clarify/Modify
- **Rationale:** Lab PA in LTPAC involves urgent clinical needs and multi-party workflows; DMEPOS PA requires coordination between facilities, suppliers, and payers with clinical documentation from LTPAC clinicians; delays impose direct patient safety risks.
- **Specific request:** Allow signed Test Requisition Form (TRF) as sufficient medical necessity documentation; standardize DMEPOS PA documentation using MDS/OASIS as evidentiary basis; prohibit removal of medically necessary DMEPOS from LTPAC residents while a PA appeal is pending.

**Topic 11: AI-Enabled PA Automation**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Clarify/Modify
- **Rationale:** AI PA tools require payer-specific policies, claims manuals, delegation rules, and business line exceptions — policy digitization still incomplete; denial rates remain high even with AI automation, with back-end denials occurring after pre-service authorization; AI tools trained on non-LTPAC populations may not be valid for older adults with multimorbidity.
- **Specific request:** Require AI-enabled PA tools used for LTPAC patients to be validated on LTPAC populations; include human-in-the-loop review, override capabilities, and audit trails; require post-market surveillance; prohibit payer AI vendors from shifting liability entirely to LTPAC providers through indemnification agreements.

**Topic 12: Medical/Pharmacy Benefit Scope Clarity for LTPAC**
- **Provision ID:** MEDICAL-VS-PHARMACY-BENEFIT, PA-DRUG-MEDICAL
- **Position:** Clarify
- **Rationale:** The medical/pharmacy benefit rubric does not map cleanly to LTPAC settings where drugs are often administered under Medicare Part A consolidated billing; dual-eligible beneficiaries' drug workflows involve simultaneous Medicare and Medicaid rules.
- **Specific request:** Publish detailed LTPAC-specific guidance clarifying scope of Prior Authorization API for Part A consolidated billing, SNF-specific drug administration, and dual-eligible beneficiary coverage.

---

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

- **S1 (require vs recommend IGs, FHIR-IG-REQUIRED):** Supports making Da Vinci CRD, DTR, PAS, CDex IGs required; urges ONC to facilitate LTPAC EHR testing environments and centralized state Medicaid FHIR questionnaire development.
- **S12 (technical challenges, PA-DRUG-MEDICAL):** Requests LTPAC-specific guidance on medical/pharmacy benefit distinction for Part A consolidated billing, SNF drug administration, and dual-eligible workflows.
- **S14 (non-Part D applicability, PA-DRUG-PHARMACY):** Supports extending NCPDP standards to Medicaid/CHIP/QHP; requests extension to all Medicare/Medicaid subcontractors beyond currently defined "impacted payers."
- **S15 (medical vs pharmacy distinction):** Requests explicit guidance on how this rubric applies to SNF consolidated billing, bundled Part A payments, and dual-eligible beneficiary drug coverage.
- **S18 (mandatory IG burden):** Acknowledges LTPAC EHR vendors need targeted support; urges inclusion in ONC innovation programs and testing environments.
- **S19 (state readiness, PA-DRUG-PHARMACY):** Notes state Medicaid agencies have not yet digitized provider manuals into FHIR questionnaires for DTR; urges CMS to support centralized FHIR questionnaire development.
- **S20 (24-hour achievable, PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS):** Supports shortened, standardized timeframes across all payer types; urges addition of emergency supply provisions for LTPAC settings.
- **S22 (NCPDP costs):** Notes 63+ payer complexity in single LTPAC facility; supports NCPDP standardization as cost-reduction mechanism; urges payer-first enforcement.
- **S25 (RTPB maturity):** Supports RTPB requirement; notes LTPAC EHR and pharmacy systems lack functionality to access/display FB/RTPB information; requests paired technical assistance for provider-side readiness.
- **S29 (which metrics, API-USAGE-METRICS):** Urges stratification by care setting, drug category, payer type, and denial reason code type (procedural vs. clinical).
- **S35 (publish aggregate):** Supports public reporting but notes aggregate plan-level reporting will obscure LTPAC disparities; recommends setting-stratified and drug-category-level reporting.
- **S37 (implementation challenges, FHIR-IG-REQUIRED):** Identifies HITAC-confirmed gaps: limited LTPAC EHR testing environments, insufficient provider awareness, incomplete state Medicaid FHIR questionnaire digitization.
- **S43 (align timeframes):** Supports alignment of CHIP FFS with Medicaid 24-hour requirement; supports uniform application across all payer types.
- **S44 (FHIR appropriate, HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS):** Supports adopting FHIR as HIPAA PA transaction standard as long-overdue modernization.
- **S47 (timeline, HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS):** Supports proposed compliance dates but requests extension and flexibility mechanisms for LTPAC technology partners with legacy systems.
- **S49 (small entity impact, HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS):** Notes LTPAC EHR and pharmacy system vendors have historically received fewer implementation resources than hospital/ambulatory EHR developers; urges targeted support.
- **S53 (phasing, HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS):** Supports phased approach with extension mechanisms for entities requiring additional time due to resource constraints.
- **S60 (versioning approach, ONC-STANDARDS-UPDATE):** Supports updated Da Vinci IG versions; requests that expiration of prior versions include advance notice and LTPAC-inclusive testing.
- **S66/S67 (general RFI — lab/DMEPOS impact):** Lab PA delays cause treatment delays and preventable hospitalizations in LTPAC; DMEPOS PA creates multi-party coordination burden; documents scenario where wheelchair can be taken from a patient during PA appeal.
- **S68/S69 (general RFI — automation):** Supports ePA automation for lab/DMEPOS but requires LTPAC population validation; human-in-the-loop review for AI tools; prohibit AI vendor liability shifting.
- **S71 (general RFI — technology gaps):** LTPAC EHR systems vary widely; many smaller providers use legacy systems without API integration; automation must be validated on LTPAC populations.
- **S73 (general RFI — workforce impact):** PA burden in LTPAC diverts direct care nurses, social workers, and administrators from patient care; staffing shortages already critical; urges CMS to track and report workforce impact by care setting.

---

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Explicitly recognize in the final rule that drug PA in LTPAC carries mandatory care obligations, retroactive coverage risk, and patient safety implications fundamentally different from community pharmacy PA.
2. Prohibit retroactive PA denials for medications administered under mandatory LTPAC care obligations; establish prospective PA submission procedures; address retroactive eligibility change interactions.
3. Publish integrated guidance clarifying how CMS-0062-P drug PA requirements interact with CMS-0057 medical PA requirements for LTPAC settings, including SNF consolidated billing, Part A bundled drug payments, and dual-eligible coverage.
4. Require payers to publish machine-readable, standardized PA routing rules including benefits determination logic, delegation rules, clinical guideline requirements, and exceptions.
5. Apply NCPDP SCRIPT, FB, and RTPB requirements to all Medicare and Medicaid subcontractors, not only currently defined "impacted payers."
6. Develop LTPAC- and LTC pharmacy-specific NCPDP SCRIPT ePA implementation guidance addressing disconnected prescribers, cycle-fill processes, and Medicare Part A consolidated billing.
7. Require that payer PA decision criteria for LTPAC patients be validated on older adults with multimorbidity, polypharmacy, and functional limitations.
8. Establish monitored payer readiness milestones with publicly available API testing environments before provider compliance requirements take effect; include LTPAC EHR and pharmacy system vendors.
9. Facilitate publicly available ePA testing environments that include LTPAC systems; support state Medicaid agencies for centralized FHIR questionnaire development.
10. Require LTPAC EHR system eligibility for ONC innovation programs with LTPAC enrollment sites and geriatric population representation; require PACIO Project FHIR IG compatibility.
11. Apply shortest clinically appropriate PA timeframes consistently across all payer types; require impacted payers to honor emergency supply provisions (minimum 72-hour supply) for LTPAC settings.
12. Establish separate electronic workflows for substantive denials versus procedural errors to maintain electronic continuity through the appeals process.
13. Require PA notices directed to legally recognized surrogate decision-makers in LTPAC; require facility-level receipt as primary notification channel.
14. Require PA metrics stratified by care setting, drug category, payer type, and denial reason code type; establish binding 90%+ automation target with financial consequences.
15. Provide targeted FHIR/HIPAA transition support for LTPAC EHR and pharmacy system vendors; preserve extension/flexibility mechanisms during HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS transition.
16. Allow signed Test Requisition Form (TRF) as sufficient medical necessity documentation for laboratory PA.
17. Standardize DMEPOS PA documentation using MDS/OASIS standards as evidentiary basis; prohibit removal of medically necessary DMEPOS during pending PA appeals.
18. Require AI-enabled PA tools for LTPAC patients to be validated on LTPAC populations with human-in-the-loop review, override capabilities, audit trails, and post-market surveillance.
19. Track and publicly report workforce impact of PA requirements in LTPAC settings by care setting, provider type, and payer.
20. Dedicate funding and technical assistance for LTPAC interoperability; integrate LTPAC into TEFCA-based ePA exchange; establish payer obligation for demographic data consistency to address ~30% PA submission failure rate.
21. Establish payer obligation to maintain patient demographic records consistent with LTPAC provider EHR data (single-source-of-truth requirement).

---

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** LTPAC-specific mandatory care obligations and retroactive PA denial risk are unaddressed; 15-year HITECH-exclusion technology gap cannot be closed by rulemaking alone; payer readiness for CMS-0057 APIs not complete until end of 2026; AI-PA tools not validated on LTPAC populations; aggregate metrics will obscure LTPAC disparities.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** PA delays are patient safety events in LTPAC (not merely administrative inconvenience); retroactive denials impose direct financial harm to facilities on thin margins; ~30% of PA submissions fail due to demographic misalignment; LTPAC EHR systems excluded from current testing environments; patients with dementia not reachable through standard notification.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** 63+ payers in a single nursing home with heterogeneous PA requirements; 65+ payer web portals and 750+ fax forms in current manual environment; only 17% hospital-to-LTPAC interoperable data exchange; LTPAC EHR vendors underrepresented in federal health IT programs; disconnected prescribers; LTC pharmacy cycle-fill workflow complexity.

---

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:**
  - 63+ payers in a single nursing home (Cleveland, OH example), all Medicare subcontractors.
  - 65+ payer web portals and 750+ payer fax forms in current manual PA environment.
  - ~30% of PA submission failures caused by demographic data misalignment between provider EHRs and payer systems.
  - Only 17% of hospitals routinely send interoperable health information to LTPAC providers; only 8% routinely receive it.
  - LTPAC patients average 8–10 medications with high PA rates for specialty drugs, antipsychotics, opioids, and biologics.
  - HITAC confirmed payer compliance with CMS-0057 APIs not expected until end of 2026.
- **Studies or research referenced:** HITAC May 7, 2026 Affordability Hearing on administrative workflows; previous Collaborative comments on HTI-2; CRUSH RFI; NIH AI Strategy RFI; CMS-0057 (2024 final rule).
- **Examples provided:** Single nursing home managing 63+ payers; wheelchair removal during PA appeal; SNF consolidated billing complexity; coagulation monitoring and infection diagnostics as urgent LTPAC lab needs; pressure-relieving mattresses and oxygen equipment as DMEPOS examples.

---

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** LTPAC providers (SNFs, home health, hospice, assisted living, CCRCs, rehabilitation), LTC pharmacies, LTPAC EHR and pharmacy system vendors, Medicare/Medicaid dual-eligible beneficiaries, cognitively impaired residents and their surrogates, LTPAC clinical and administrative workforce
- **Economic implications:** Direct financial harm from retroactive PA denials on thin-margin facilities; significant workforce diversion from patient care to PA administration; potential major savings from demographic misalignment resolution (eliminating ~30% electronic PA failures)
- **Technical feasibility:** LTPAC sector faces 15-year HITECH investment gap; many smaller LTPAC providers use legacy systems without API integration; publicly available testing environments exclude LTPAC systems; feasibility contingent on dedicated investment and phased payer-first enforcement
- **Patient care impact:** Very high — PA delays are patient safety events in mandatory-care settings; cognitively impaired residents cannot advocate for themselves; medication discontinuities and care gaps directly worsen outcomes for already medically complex patients

---

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Mixed (strongly supportive of rule goals with extensive sector-specific modification requests)
- **Tone:** Professional, technical, collaborative, advocacy-focused
- **Priority level:** High

---

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "Affordability, modernization, and consumer choice cannot be achieved for older Americans without intentionally designing solutions for LTPAC. We face 63+ payers in a single facility, a 15-year technology investment gap from HITECH exclusion, mandatory care obligations that make prior authorization delays a patient safety issue, and only 17% of hospitals sending interoperable data to us." — Context: Shelly Spiro's HITAC testimony, framing the overarching LTPAC challenge.
2. "Drug prior authorization in LTPAC is categorically different from community pharmacy prior authorization." — Context: Core framing principle for all LTPAC-specific recommendations; addresses the absence of this recognition in the proposed rule.
3. "Prior authorization delays are patient safety events in LTPAC. Unlike community settings where a prescription can be withheld pending payer determination, LTPAC facilities have a mandatory care obligation." — Context: Establishing why PA timeframes carry patient safety implications specific to LTPAC.
4. "Standards without transparent rules will not eliminate manual workarounds." — Context: Arguing that NCPDP standardization must be paired with machine-readable, standardized payer PA routing rules to solve the workflow problem, not just the data problem.

---

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **IMPLEMENTATION-TIMELINE** — Urges payer-first enforcement with monitored readiness milestones before provider compliance is required; supports compliance dates with flexibility mechanisms for LTPAC technology partners; notes payer compliance with CMS-0057 APIs not complete until end of 2026.
- [x] **COST-RESOURCES** — 15-year HITECH exclusion technology gap; thin-margin facilities absorbing retroactive denial costs; requests dedicated funding and technical assistance for LTPAC EHR/pharmacy vendors.
- [x] **PROVIDER-BURDEN** — 63+ payers per facility; 65+ web portals and 750+ fax forms; ~30% submission failures from demographic misalignment; workforce diversion from direct care to PA administration.
- [x] **HEALTH-EQUITY** — LTPAC patients (elderly, dual-eligible, cognitively impaired, high multimorbidity) are among those most harmed by PA barriers; aggregate metrics obscure LTPAC disparities; cognitively impaired residents cannot advocate through standard processes.
- [x] **TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY** — LTPAC EHR systems excluded from testing environments; disconnected prescriber workflows; LTC pharmacy cycle-fill processes; legacy systems without API integration; 15-year HITECH gap.
- [x] **STANDARDS-MATURITY** — Supports NCPDP SCRIPT 2023011, FB, RTPB, and Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS/CDex; identifies state Medicaid FHIR questionnaire digitization gap; urges PACIO Project FHIR IG compatibility.
- [x] **PATIENT-ACCESS** — PA delays are patient safety events in mandatory-care settings; medication discontinuities directly worsen outcomes; emergency supply provisions essential; cognitively impaired residents require surrogate notification.
- [x] **STAKEHOLDER-COORDINATION** — Multi-party complexity (facilities, suppliers, payers, prescribers, pharmacies); TEFCA integration for LTPAC QHINs; coordination between CMS-0062-P and CMS-0057 frameworks; state Medicaid MCO policy digitization inconsistency.
- [x] **MEDICAL-VS-PHARMACY-BENEFIT** — LTPAC drug administration under Part A consolidated billing does not map to the medical/pharmacy benefit rubric; dual-eligible beneficiaries face simultaneous Medicare and Medicaid PA frameworks.
- [x] **TRANSPARENCY** — Strongly supports PA metrics reporting but requires care-setting stratification and drug-category breakdown; binding automation targets with financial consequences.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** — Disconnected prescriber workflows; LTC pharmacy cycle-fill processes; multi-party DMEPOS and lab PA workflows; retroactive eligibility changes during episodes of care; electronic appeals continuity gap.
- [x] **VENDOR-ECOSYSTEM** — LTPAC EHR and pharmacy system vendors historically excluded from federal health IT resources, testing environments, and ONC innovation programs; need targeted implementation support for NCPDP and FHIR standards.
